Theme

Latin word

ille

ille, illa, illud

pronoun

the former (with hic, the latter); he, that man (there); the former; that; (plural) those; the famous, the well-known

In this lexicon

  • former

    the recommended word · classical · Sall. Cat. 54.2: ille mānsuētūdine et misericordiā clārus factus, huic sevēritās dignitātem addiderat

  • he

    also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: ut illum amēs

  • that

    the recommended word · classical · Catull. 4.1: phasēlus ille, quem vidētis; Cic. Fam. 7.18.2: cētera bellē; illud mīror

  • the

    also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 22: Mēdēa illa (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 50: honestum illud Solōnis est (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Caesar beneficiīs ac mūnificentiā magnus habēbātur, integritāte vītae Catō. ille mānsuētūdine et misericordiā clārus factus, huic sevēritās dignitātem addiderat

    Caesar was thought great for his kindnesses and his generosity, Cato for the integrity of his life. The former had won fame by his gentleness and mercy; the latter’s strictness had added to his standingSall. Cat. 54.2
